hints: Look first at W on the left. Notice how wide those two cells are, with thick banded walls and no black nuclei inside.
Now compare U and V on the right. Which cells have a large black nucleus, and which cells have perforated end walls (sieve plates) but no nucleus?
walkthrough:
**Spot the xylem in W**

Start with the easiest clue. W shows two very wide, hollow tubes with lignified thickening and no nuclei or cytoplasm.

That is classic for dead, water-conducting tubes. So W = xylem vessel elements.

**Tell companion cells from sieve tubes**

Phloem works as a pair. The sieve tube element does the transporting, so it has sieve plates with pores but has lost its nucleus. The companion cell keeps its nucleus and dense cytoplasm to control the sieve tube.

In the diagram, V labels the narrow cells with clear black nuclei. U labels the narrow cells with sieve plates and no nuclei. So V = companion cells and U = phloem sieve tube elements.

**Match to the table**

We have V = companion cells, U = phloem sieve tube elements, W = xylem vessel elements.

That combination is exactly row B.

options.A: Swaps all three. U is not the companion cell and W is not phloem, W is clearly the wide lignified xylem.
options.B: Correct. V has nuclei so is companion cells, U has sieve plates with no nucleus so is sieve tube elements, W is wide lignified tubes so is xylem vessel elements.
options.C: U is not the companion cell. The nucleated cells are V, while U is the enucleate cell with sieve plates.
options.D: W cannot be companion cells as it is wide, dead and lignified, and U cannot be xylem as it is narrow with sieve plates.
